reading_plan: Source title: System-scale design and analysis of desalination systems for meeting water needs of data centers. Source type: peer_reviewed_paper. The PDF is a two-column Water Research article, with a graphical abstract, nomenclature, citation-dense introduction, numbered equations, an input table, and results that alternate between prose and multi-panel graphics. I take shorter steps through definitions, modeling choices, and figure-heavy comparisons, and longer steps where the argument runs continuously. Locations use the PDF’s printed page numbers.

reading_path.location: p. 1, Highlights, graphical abstract, and Abstract
reading_path.moves: Frames the problem, declares the comparison and metrics, then previews results and the application to local stress.

claims.text: Growth in high-performance computing and AI intensifies energy use and increases freshwater demand for thermal management.

The study evaluates two-stage RO, MVC and hybrid systems to supply freshwater below 500 ppm TDS, using 5,000 ppm brackish water, 35,000 ppm seawater and produced water at or above 50,000 ppm, with conventional, minimum and zero liquid discharge scenarios.

support.text: The graphical abstract depicts alternate saline feeds, desalination, delivery of product water to a data center, and separate pathways for the concentrate.

claims.text: Across feed salinities the transition to MLD and ZLD raises recovery by 4–220%, with specific energy and water cost rising by more than 12% and 15%, respectively, in the abstract’s summary.

support.text: The abstract reports 736 L/1,000 kg feed, 9.4 kWh/m³ permeate and $3.2/m³ for a seawater hybrid with MLD; for 50,000 ppm produced water with MVC and MLD it reports 753 L/1,000 kg feed, 36 kWh/m³ and $10.4/m³.

claims.text: SWUI is introduced to quantify local stress implications. Representative projections rise from 2023 to 2030 and range from mild to substantial; higher MLD recovery can cut SWUI by 40% in a stressed setting despite the energy and cost tradeoff.

support.text: The Highlights flag SWUI above 7 with evaporative cooling.

reading_path.meaning: The abstract establishes two scales of inquiry: how the water plant performs and what its deployment implies for a data center’s regional water use.
